title: Istio 1.31 Adds Agentgateway Waypoints and Moves Release Artifacts off Google Cloud
gist: Istio 1.31 lets teams run Solo.io-donated agentgateway as an L7 waypoint in ambient mesh for agent and MCP traffic, and the project is moving all release infrastructure from Google Cloud to AWS because of changes in its funding model. Users of the old registries must migrate before retirement in December.

insights.claim: Istio 1.31 can run agentgateway as a Layer 7 waypoint proxy in ambient mesh via the istio-agentgateway-waypoint GatewayClass, extending the experimental gateway-only integration from 1.30.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Service mesh incumbents are absorbing agent traffic management, so standalone agent-gateway vendors face platform competition.

insights.claim: Agentgateway is a Rust data plane built for agent traffic, donated by Solo.io to the Linux Foundation, handling protocols like Model Context Protocol alongside ordinary HTTP.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Vendor donation to the Linux Foundation signals agent-traffic infrastructure is being standardized as open source.

insights.claim: Waypoint traffic shifting is alpha: a canary waypoint can receive a configurable share of new connections via label and annotation, but established connections are not moved, so long-lived connections can delay the split.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Maturity caveat: agentgateway waypoints are early, so production adoption is likely gradual.
insights.locator: That shifting mechanism is new too

themes.theme: Istio's infrastructure move from Google Cloud to AWS

insights.claim: Istio is migrating all its infrastructure from Google Cloud to AWS due to changes in its funding model, and stops publishing images and Helm charts to Google Cloud; old registries retire in December.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Open-source infrastructure sponsorship credits are shifting between clouds, a signal of cloud-vendor funding priorities for CNCF projects.
insights.quote: this year, Istio is migrating all of our infrastructure from Google Cloud Platform to Amazon Web Services due to changes in our funding model

insights.claim: Scream tests disabling old endpoints run 13 October (15:00-18:00 UTC) and 8-9 December, and image-signature verifiers must handle key rotation to istio-key-v2.pub from 1.31.1.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Deadlines for users of Istio images to avoid outages and verification failures.

insights.claim: Istio chose Docker Hub over GHCR because GHCR has undocumented limits the project would easily exceed given its usage.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Rate limits of container registries are a hidden constraint for high-traffic open-source projects.

insights.claim: A new zoneAwareLbSetting lets Envoy prefer endpoints in the same availability zone and spill over automatically when local capacity runs out, replacing static percentages in localityLbSetting.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Zone-aware routing cuts cross-AZ data transfer costs for large meshes.

insights.claim: A fips-140-3 COMPLIANCE_POLICY value restricts TLS to 1.2+ with FIPS-compliant ciphers, but Go components must also be built with Go 1.24+ and GOFIPS140 set, so the runtime setting alone is insufficient.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: FIPS support matters for regulated and government buyers adopting the mesh.
